questions.q: What causes the phases of the moon?
questions.a: We see changing amounts of the sunlit half of the moon as it circles the earth each month.

questions.q: What is a new moon and a full moon?
questions.a: New moon: the moon lies between earth and sun, its lit side faces away - not visible. Full moon: earth lies between, the whole lit side shows.

questions.q: How long does the moon take to complete its phases?

questions.a: When the moon comes between the sun and earth and its shadow falls on earth, hiding the sun.

questions.q: Why should we never look at a solar eclipse directly?
questions.a: The sun's rays can burn and permanently damage the retina.
When the earth comes between the sun and moon, casting its shadow on the full moon.

Name two festivals linked to the phases of the moon.
questions.a: Diwali falls on a new moon night; Guru Nanak Jayanti or Buddha Purnima on full moon.

questions.q: Why do many Indian calendars follow lunar months?
questions.a: Festivals and farming traditions track the moon's phases month by month.

questions.q: How is Ekadashi related to the moon?
questions.a: It falls on the eleventh day after new moon and full moon - tied to the lunar cycle.
A human-made object launched to circle the earth - like INSAT, IRS or the ISS.

questions.q: Name two uses of artificial satellites.
questions.a: Communication (TV, phone) and weather monitoring; also navigation and mapping.

questions.q: How do satellites stay in orbit without falling?
questions.a: Their forward speed balances the earth's gravity pulling them down.
